message: Rede D'Or Investment Thesis, cover with team names and head.
layout_trick: Full-bleed surgical photo with navy duotone overlay, logo bottom-left and team credits in small type; title is just the logo lockup.

message: Healthcare is a US$11.34tn, acyclic, inelastic sector driven by aging and rising R&D spend.
layout_trick: Six-panel grid under three numbered roman-numeral headers (I/II/III), each header with a thin blue rule and a grey chart subtitle; big-number box with dashed connector tree to sector segments.

message: Brazil: low private insurance penetration (23.3%), extreme income inequality, and >60% of beds are private.
layout_trick: Donut with a grey trapezoid 'zoom' wedge that opens into the detail bar chart (top 1% earns more than bottom 95%), a visual drill-down linking two charts.

message: Brazil is aging and the healthcare sector is consolidating via M&A.
layout_trick: Population pyramid mirrored left/right in two shades of blue next to a 60+ projection bar chart, with a dashed callout box stating the key delta (6% to 20%).

message: Payors' expenses convert into providers' revenue: P&L of the plan operator and of the hospital side by side.
layout_trick: Two stacked mini waterfalls (payer P&L on top, hospital P&L below) joined by a full-width teal banner 'Payor's Expenses convert into the Provider's Revenue' as the hinge.

message: Insurance sector is corporate-led, concentrated in a few players and hit by macro (unemployment, MLR).
layout_trick: Three columns I/II/III each with a different chart type (donut, treemap of market share, combo bars+line) under one consistent header style; COVID callout on the line.

message: Private hospital sector is highly fragmented: only 10% of market, top players hold little share.
layout_trick: Treemap of listed hospital companies' market share with dashed callout 'The 3 largest players have only 10% of the market' and HHI box.

message: Rede D'Or is the largest hospital services provider in Brazil, 70+ hospitals in 13 states, 50 oncology clinics.
layout_trick: Blue 'About the company' tab with icon+short facts at top left, Brazil map with operating states highlighted, curved wave timeline across the bottom and donut/column charts in grey right panel.

message: SulAmerica is a 129-year-old insurer, most expensive and most penetrated, bought by Rede D'Or.
layout_trick: Same template as the company slide (tab + map + curved milestone ribbon timeline) reused for the acquired company, making the two profiles directly comparable.

message: RDOR3 HOLD: DCF upside 18.8%, IRR 19.4%, current price R$30.33 vs target R$36.
layout_trick: Dark navy slide: price history line with dashed target-price line and three honeycomb hexagons stacking DCF/IRR/Current Price as key stats.

message: Three thesis pillars: best player in sector, strong revenue growth, DCF says Hold.
layout_trick: Roman-numeral hexagons on a curved vertical thread on dark navy; the active pillar is bright and the other two fade, repeated as a divider before each thesis section.

message: Rede D'Or has best-in-sector occupancy, EBITDA margin and NPS lift after acquisitions.
layout_trick: NPS bars before/after acquisition per hospital plus grey zoom panel with competitor logos and score (Vila Nova Star 94, Albert Einstein 86) as external benchmark.

message: High bargain power with insurers: readjustments above IPCA even when Amil dropped Rede D'Or.
layout_trick: Fake browser-window screenshot of the G1 headline embedded as evidence next to the chart of beneficiaries lost, plus dashed key-stat box (readjustment 7.7% vs IPCA 4.4%).

message: High bargain power with suppliers: materials/medicine share of COGS falls with scale.
layout_trick: Photo of sell-side analyst with direct quote in a grey card used as qualitative proof beside the margin line chart.

message: Management is experienced and aligned: founder as chairman, pay in line with sector, Moll family holds 47%.
layout_trick: Executive rows with photos alternating left/right on grey bars, plus dashed boxes of logos showing where the board came from (healthcare / finance).

layout_trick: Brazil map in blue shades with brand logos (UDI, Esperanca, Sao Rafael) pinned by dashed leaders, next to maturation bars Rede D'Or vs ANAHP.

message: Rede D'Or has better clinical outcomes than ANAHP peers in infections and ICU stay.
layout_trick: 2x2 grid of four small line/bar charts, each comparing Rede D'Or (dark blue) vs ANAHP (teal) with same legend and axis style for fast reading.

message: Rede D'Or keeps margin leadership because COGS per revenue and per bed are lower than peers.
layout_trick: Three-block layout where the roman header states the finding and the sub-line gives the unit (COGS per hospital bed).

layout_trick: Two bar series (initial plan vs new plan) with dashed box around TBD bars in grey and a grey trapezoid callout listing reasons for the delay.
